Swaps still lean towards a peak in rates. A firm jobs number would challenge that, lifting front-end yields and supporting the currency, while a rise in unemployment would reinforce bets on easing by 2027. The contrast between strong wage growth and rising layoffs creates two-way risk for Australian bank stocks and rate-sensitive retailers, especially given the job cuts at David Jones and Bunnings. Watch the jobless rate on Thursday more closely than the headline jobs figure. --- Australia now has wages, interest rates and unemployment all rising together, which leaves the RBA choosing between the pay data and the layoff headlines. items.title: TSMC reportedly demands cash up front from AI chip clients amid circular financing fears
items.summary: If confirmed, the move would be a vote of caution about AI customer finances from the company with the clearest view of chip demand. That would add weight to the circular financing debate that has hung over AI stocks this month. Custom chip designers and smaller AI players with stretched balance sheets would face tighter cash flow and could lose capacity to better-funded rivals. For TSMC, the policy would strengthen its pricing power and reduce its credit risk, a positive for the stock and for Taiwan’s tech-heavy market. Watch for any confirmation or denial from TSMC, which would set how seriously the report is taken. --- While Nvidia extends credit to the AI boom, TSMC is reportedly asking its customers to show the money first, and that difference says a lot about who carries the risk. Ken "Bulldog" Sanders, a standout on the first three Milwaukee Brewers teams who stayed in the area after his playing days, died at 85. The St. Louis-born Sanders spent 10 seasons in Major League Baseball, including the first three seasons of the Milwaukee Brewers' existence from 1970 through 1972, when he had a 2.21 ERA and 61 saves. He continued living in the Milwaukee area after his time in the big leagues. "Bulldog" – a nickname bestowed by former Brewers manager Dave Bristol – led the American League with 31 saves in 1971 and posted a 1.91 ERA and 1.064 WHIP, even earning MVP votes that season.

Drought conditions and low reservoir levels are affecting the renewable power source. The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration. Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an extreme, prolonged drought in the Colorado River Basin has resulted in dangerously low water levels in the Southwest’s two largest reservoirs, affecting the availability of this power source.

Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things. Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.

The Advertising Standards Authority says the adverts by online healthcare provider Voy made misleading claims. Five adverts by online healthcare provider Voy have been banned by the watchdog for making misleading claims linked to low testosterone in men. It said they were misleading as they linked common symptoms such as irritability and fatigue to low testosterone. After snow fell across northern England and southern Scotland on Tuesday, is there more on the way? The Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson "because he's already so famous". Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in picking actor Robert Pattinson for the role of James Bond in the next 007 film. Speaking onstage at an event in California, the Amazon CEO said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in a number of blockbuster films including Batman and the Twilight franchise - "because he's already so famous". The role has typically gone to an actor who is not as well-known at the time of casting. But Bezos said in screen tests, "it was so obvious he is James Bond".

Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey - who helped the Gunners win the Double in 1970-71 - has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals. He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee. "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement. "All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.

The International Ice Hockey Federation said Tuesday that it has been the target of a cyberattack. The nature of attack was not mentioned, though as of Tuesday night its website remained offline. Tiger Woods will return to golf at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas next month, his first 72-hole tournament since 2024. The 15-time major champion's last appearance in a PGA Tour event was at the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut . Prior to that, he completed the 2024 Masters, finishing in 60th place. Woods then missed the entire 2025 season due to a ruptured left Achilles tendon suffered while training for the Masters. The Hero World Challenge is an invitational tournament hosted by Woods himself, featuring a select field of 20 players. The 72-hole event has no cut, and participants are required to walk the course, as carts are not permitted.

Currently, the top four teams in the 12-team playoff get a first-round bye while Nos. 5-12 play each other across four first-round games. It comes after Burnham confirmed he would set out options to recast the UK's long-term relationship with Europe next month, in the wake of a summit this week to unveil a series of deals to "reset" relations.
